questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A country that speaks fluent English so I can speak with everyone while simultaneously improving my English. Additionally, I wanted an amazing experience traveling across the world and experiencing a new culture, which would also give me opportunities to travel, which there are plenty of.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not easy at all. Previous reports you might have read stated that it was extremely easy to find accommodation, but that is not the case anymore at least. Probably changed due to Covid. So I would recommend if you want to find a stay you need to come early.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not. They cannot help with a longer stay. You can contact Student One if you really need to find a place to stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was actually very difficult to find housing off campus. Took a while, and we got lucky.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get in Brisbane in good time otherwise, you will clash with all the other exchange students looking for a stay. Also, renting apartments requires a minimum lease of 6 months, so I would look for rooms using flatmates or something similar. I would recommend to stay in hostels when you arrive. You get to meet a lot of other exchange students who are in the same situation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 5You can use StudentOne if you need a place to stay. You live with many other exchange students and share an apartment of 4-5 people. It is a private practice, so QUT has nothing to do with them.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get your info in e-mails. You receive passwords etc. and then you can always contact the student administration for international students if needed (they were very helpful and respond fast).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student international administration. Find their e-mail online if you have not received it yet.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. You do it online. They give you a deadline and you can easily register for your classes online.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you read the information they send over in PDF-files. It will answer a lot of your questions otherwise just contact them. They are extremely helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I mean the academic level is very much subpar to what we are used to. However, it is probably hard to find an academic challenge since most people who are on exchange say it is a lot easier than at home. Also, you just have to pass classes. If you only want to go for an academic challenge, QUT or Australia, in general, is probably not for you.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were Bachelor level. Extremely easy to pass, and since you have no incentive to get a higher grade just enjoy your stay instead.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. Lectures and tutorials. However, most of the tutorials are shorter and also just go over the answers in the problem set given for that week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Market Structure and Regulation
Applied Econometrics
Fundamentals of Finance
Corporate Finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fundamentals of Finance and Corporate Finance, if you are interested in Finance. However, you have learned some of the curricula already.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Alcohol and cigarettes are extremely expensive.  Generally, it is more expensive to just live the same life in Australia as it is in Denmark. Everything is a bit more expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol and cigarettes. Fitness is also more expensive
Coffee is however very affordable and cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs to choose from. Much more to do in Australia in terms of sport etc., because of the nicer weather

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The surf club is great since they host some trips to Byron Bay. They sell out fast when they come online, however, so be ready. It is for beginners and everyone just has a good time there. A bit expensive, but worth it.

There are so many clubs to choose from. You can just google it. There have to be at least 50 clubs, and probably more. I would recommend that you find some of these clubs and attend at least in the beginning as you will meet a lot of people that way.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As stated above, just join some of these clubs you are interested in for social interactions and to expand your network. A lot of exchange students also join these clubs, and they are in the same boat as you so don't be shy. Just go out with a positive attitude, and you will meet some great people. Additionally, Australians are a lot easier to befriend than your average Dane.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I loved going on road trips. It is quite easy to rent a car and just drive. Important remember to get an international license from your local municipality institution otherwise you will not be allowed to drive and rent cars. I did a lot of hiking, going to beaches up north or to the gold coast.  You can always chill at the fake beach in South Bank aswell.

 Also, go out a lot to the party, Get drunk on goon (card box wine) instead as drinking a lot of beer or hard liquor will ruin your finances.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Their culture is similar to ours, however they are a bit more laid back.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Be extremely social for at least the first month. If you are hungover and don't feel like going out, do it anyways. Social bonding at the start of your exchange is important and will help you meet even more people.
Obviously, be there the first week of orientation. You get to meet a lot of people there. And probably a lot of Danes as well.
Stay in hostels in the beginning.
Join a lot of clubs.
Get a group chat going, and meet with the people from your universities down there as it might help you make other friends as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They love to swear. It is all good. They are a lot more open and friendly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Laid back and chill just gives you good vibes on an exchange, which is more geared towards having great experiences.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of Danes and Norwegians there, but make sure you also get some local friends and other exchange students as friends.
Open up your comfort zone.
Don't worry too much about the money. It will be expensive, and you will go out to eat, drink more, and have other experiences. It will be worth it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot can be done online or at other times. They have some assignments that count toward your grade. Make sure you make a good effort on them so your final exam is more manageable if you have not studied as much for that.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences, friends and personal growth.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving to a new country can be difficult. You might get lonely and homesick at times. Relax. You will make some great friends there and have memories for life. The exchange is over quickly. Make sure to enjoy and savor every minute of it

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Get Optus instead of Vodafone. Their connection is faster, wider, and better.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
